readings.title: Prayer at Holy Matrimony
readings.text: O eternal God, who hast brought into unity those who were sundered, and hast ordained for them an indissoluble bond of love; who didst bless Isaac and Rebecca, and didst make them heirs of thy promise: Bless also these thy servants, N. and N., guiding them unto every good work. For thou art a merciful God, who lovest mankind, and unto thee do we ascribe glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now, and ever, and unto ages of ages.

readings.title: Prayer for concord
readings.text: O Lord our God, who in thy saving providence didst vouchsafe by thy presence in Cana of Galilee to declare marriage honourable: Do thou, the same Lord, now also maintain in peace and concord thy servants, N. and N., whom it hath pleased thee to join together. Cause their marriage to be honourable. Preserve their bed blameless. Mercifully grant that they may live together in purity; and enable them to attain to a ripe old age, walking in thy commandments with a pure heart.

readings.title: Forgiveness
readings.text: Since He might indeed, even without this, forgive thee all thine offenses; but He wills thee hereby also to receive a benefit; affording thee on all sides innumerable occasions of gentleness and love to man, casting out what is brutish in thee, and quenching wrath, and in all ways cementing thee to him who is thine own member.

readings.title: What does the first marriage prayer ask for?

paragraphs.text: The prayer associates marriage with a bond of love and recalls Isaac and Rebecca. It asks blessing and guidance in good works for the couple. Its language belongs to the existing marriage office rather than a new prayer composed for this resource.

readings.title: What does concord mean in the marriage prayer?

paragraphs.text: Concord means peace and harmony between the couple. The prayer connects marriage with Christ’s presence at Cana and asks for faithfulness and a long shared life. It expresses these themes within the source’s sacramental prayer.
